summary: Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as Principal (1971) and Director (1988–2001) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, President of the Association of Indian Universities, and Chancellor of Sanchi University.

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (-2014), later holding postdoctoral positions at the University of Bonn and MPIWG.

Loden Sherab Dagyab is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Tenzin Gyatso. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966) and joined the University of Bonn in 1966.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche. He also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology and studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from Punjab University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He directed the International Academy of Indian Culture and chaired the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (2014–2017) and ICHR (~2014–2017).
Longlian was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from approximately 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1962–1967). She served as curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and taught at Humboldt University (~1993–1998) and the Free University of Berlin (1994).

Lori Meeks is a Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Columbia and Princeton, the latter under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1998–2003). She was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Southern California in ~2004.

Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Peradeniya and University of London, she served as Associate Professor of History at Peradeniya (~1960–1980) and faculty member at the University of Colombo (~1980–1994).

Lothar Ledderose, a sinologist, art historian, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Tokyo, Princeton, Harvard, and Cologne. He was Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Lothar von Falkenhausen works in history, archaeology, and sinology. Educated at Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard (PhD ~1982–1988), he joined the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, serving as Full Professor and Associate Director (2004–2011).

Louis Dumont was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss and Walther Schubring. He held posts at the University of Oxford (1951–1955) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences from 1955.

Louis Finot was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar trained at the École Nationale des Chartes. He served as the first director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1898) and taught at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from approximately 1977 to 2007.

Louis H. Gray specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton University and Columbia University (PhD) and held positions at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (Associate Professor of Philosophy, 1921).

Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal and Gaston Paris. He was professor and chairman of Latin philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at the EPHE. He held posts at the EPHE (~1928–1966) and the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1937–1966), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1954–1966).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern, among others. He was Professor at Ghent University (1893–1929) and the Free University of Brussels (~1921–1935).
